summary: The 2D screening label is not_2d_applicable, and the deterministic gate set simulation_allowed=false and comparison_valid=false. Studio did not run: simulation status is 'skipped' because a custom experiment needs 1-128 blocks and a power_w object, and the extraction supplied an empty floorplan and empty power map. No Studio result exists, so there is no numerical comparison and no replication claim. The paper's selected scenario is the non-equal initial temperature case of thermal-aware GA task assignment on a quad-core out-of-order CPU (Section 5.3.2, Figure 9). The reported observable is an approximate maximum inter-core temperature difference of about 8 C per hyper-period, read from text and excluding the first hyper-period. It comes from a transient HotSpot study over 10 hyper-periods (about 14 s) with scheduling feedback, which is a different regime, aggregation (inter-core spread rather than peak or mean temperature) and boundary condition from any steady 2D run. A custom 2D steady run would also have no transient trace. The final verdict is that the scenario is not reproducible or comparable in Studio from the published information. Qualitatively, the paper's finding is that temperature-driven workload allocation reduces core-to-core thermal imbalance. A static floorplan solve cannot test that mechanism, because the optimizer and controller act on task assignment, not on geometry or package parameters. The evidence validation also flagged that no evidence items have a valid page or pinned asset locator, there is no cited steady or transient regime for the observable, and the adversarial and independent reviews were unresolved or not approved. No external artifacts were found (checked_no_links), so the claims are unverified against code or data.
limitations: Studio was not run; there is no simulated output, so no numerical comparison to the reported ~8 C inter-core spread is possible or valid.
Mismatch: no block floorplan geometry (x, y, width, height) for cores, L2 caches or other blocks is published, so a 2D layout would have to be invented.
Mismatch: Table 1 gives per-task leakage and dynamic power, not per-block power, and no mapping rule or tabulated per-hyper-period task-to-core assignment is published.
Mismatch in regime: the original study is transient (10 hyper-periods, about 14 s) with thermal feedback into task assignment, whereas a custom 2D run would be steady with no transient trace.

Mismatch in observable and aggregation: the paper's ~8 C is an approximate maximum inter-core difference per hyper-period read from text, excluding the first hyper-period; it is not a peak, mean or steady-state temperature at a defined location.
Mismatch in boundary and package assumptions: only a 45 C ambient is reported; HotSpot package, heat sink, TIM, die thickness, material properties and R/C values are missing.
The GA optimizer and per-period EDF thermal-aware scheduling controller have no counterpart in a static Studio solve.

Evidence items lack valid page or pinned asset locators, and the adversarial code, parameters, config and data checks and independent page review are unresolved; no repository, code or gem5/McPAT/HotSpot configs are available.
Initial core temperatures (65.48, 49.77, 45.82, 51.86 C) and the ~8 C spread are text-derived and not digitized from Figures 9 and 10; the spread is stated only approximately.
No exact replication is claimed; this assessment is limited to the gate outcome and qualitative observations.
